comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from Utrecht University's current official Bachelor Sociologie overview, prospective-student curriculum, current-student curriculum and progression pages, all checked 2026-09-28. The current-student curriculum fixes the 180-EC structure as a 75-EC compulsory major, 60-EC major-choice space and 45-EC profile space. The generic normalized target cp-000369 (registry row 382, source_provider_id 1015O5898, languages_json=["NLD"]) names no formal route. The prospective curriculum recommends three coherent internal pathways in this order: Sociology and Social Research, Contemporary Social Problems, and Analysing Digital Societies. No target-specific evidence distinguishes among them, so Sociology and Social Research is selected by neutral official-order tie-break before UCR fit is considered. The compulsory 75 EC are instantiated as the seven fixed first-year sociology/methods/social-problems/inequality/policy/research courses (52.5 EC), Advanced Sociological Theory (7.5 EC), and the 15-EC Bachelorproject Sociologie. The selected route's 60-EC major-choice package uses Introductie gedragswetenschappen, Practicum data-analyse, Beleids- en evaluatieonderzoek, Theory Constructing and Statistical Modelling, Measurement and Modelling with Social Data, Social Networks in Theory and Empirical Research, Doing a Qualitative Research Project, and Familiesociologie (eight 7.5-EC courses). The public page presents these as current courses and recommends Sociology and Social Research as a coherent path; where the page does not prescribe one unique package, the methodologically oriented courses are selected before UCR fit and the first-listed relevant options break ties. The genuine 45-EC profile space remains open rather than being invented. Thus 75 + 60 + 45 = 180 EC, and the comparator is fixed independently of UCR course availability.

alternatives.label: Sociology and Social Research
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is anchored by five Sociology courses and a three-course quantitative/qualitative methods sequence, with political science, economics, psychology, history, philosophy, law, diversity and communication providing the broad social-science context of Utrecht’s first-listed Sociology and Social Research pathway. The official pathway name therefore accurately describes the whole 24-course programme.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Utrecht University’s broad Bachelor Sociologie and its neutrally selected first-listed Sociology and Social Research pathway: a sociology-led curriculum combining classical and contemporary theory, inequality and social relations with quantitative and qualitative research, political and economic perspectives, and evidence-based engagement with public problems.
progression: BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD211, BENECON312 (semester 6), BENLEAD312, BENECON311 (semester 4) and BENLEAD311 (semester 5), which formally require it. HCBGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes HCBPSYC314 (semester 4), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Introduction to Sociology, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Research Methods & Statistics, Histories of Gender, Social Psychology) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Public Economics, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Econometrics) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Sociology of Digital Societies
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains five Sociology courses and a methods backbone, but its distinctive nine-course data/AI/media cluster makes digital society—not general policy or inequality—the organising domain. The label follows the programme’s own named direction while accurately reflecting the UCR curriculum.
alternatives.concept: A distinct UCR route generated by the programme’s explicit Analysing Digital Societies direction and its direct interest in whether social media creates new forms of friendship: it retains the shared sociology and research-methods core while concentrating on data science, machine learning, neural networks, databases, media, communication and the social power of algorithms.
progression: BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENECON312 (semester 6), which formally requires it. DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes DISDATA311 (semester 4), which formally requires it. BENENTR211 (semester 4, formally requiring BENGATE102) is scheduled after BENGATE102 (semester 2). Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1/level-2 courses (Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice, Foundations of Comparative Politics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Mathematical Methods, Qualitative Research Methodology) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Persuasive Communication, Media & Race, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Econometrics) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced technical and applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: The official programme separately recommends Analysing Digital Societies (16109), supported by a direct social-media-and-friendship interest (16098) and curricular topics in social-network analysis and digital data (16122, 16133). This route replaces nine courses from the closest match with data-science, AI, database and media/communication study, changing 67.5 EC and exceeding the required 30-EC/4-course distinction floor.

alternatives.label: Contemporary Social Problems and Public Policy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme retains the common sociology and research core, while its replacement cluster and retained public-economics, law, politics, inequality and negotiation courses organise the curriculum around analysing contemporary social problems and evaluating public responses. The label combines the programme’s own named direction with the main applied emphasis visible in the completed UCR curriculum.
alternatives.concept: A distinct UCR route generated by the programme’s explicit Contemporary Social Problems direction and direct interests in government responses and evidence-based solutions: it retains the shared sociology and methods core while foregrounding inequality, justice, political institutions, public economics, youth extremism, media power and policy communication.
progression: BENGATE102 in semester 2 precedes the semester-4/6 courses that require it; introductory sociology, politics, communication, psychology, methods and gender/history courses precede advanced sociological theory, public economics, negotiation, youth-extremism and econometrics work. Personal & Professional Development remains in Year 1, and every course is offered in its assigned semester for the fixed Fall-2026 cohort.
alternatives.distinctness: The official programme separately recommends Contemporary Social Problems (16108), reinforced by direct interests in government responses and evidence-based solutions (16100, 16106). Relative to the closest match, this route replaces four courses—30 EC—with The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Law, Society & Justice and Media & Race, creating the minimum permitted but academically material shift toward public problems, justice and policy communication. It is also materially distinct from the digital route.

candidates.label: Contemporary Social Problems and Public Policy

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the first-listed Sociology and Social Research direction and thirteen broad direct interests covering sociological explanation, inequality, families and neighbourhoods, religion, friendship, remote work, safety, empirical evidence, social change, group differences, quantitative research and institutions (16091-16097, 16099, 16101-16105, plus stable direction 16107). The remaining generator-eligible evidence forms two coherent directions explicitly recommended by the programme: Contemporary Social Problems (16100, 16106, 16108) and Analysing Digital Societies (16098, 16109). Both pass the evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility gates: the former foregrounds policy, inequality, law, media and public responses to social problems; the latter foregrounds social media, data, algorithms and media power. Each has a feasible 24-course UCR schedule with at least six level-300 courses. The contemporary-problems route differs from the closest match by exactly four courses (30 EC), while the digital route differs by nine courses (67.5 EC); the additional routes are also materially distinct from each other. All nineteen generator-eligible rows are assigned and the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: All three UCR alternatives include substantial sociological theory and research-methods study. The comparator additionally offers dedicated courses in measurement and modelling with social data, family sociology, social-network analysis and a credited bachelor project that UCR does not reproduce at the same depth; related UCR courses are shown only where their content is a defensible match.

Utrecht structures the degree as a 75-EC compulsory major, a 60-EC major-choice pathway and 45 EC of profile space. UCR instead combines 24 fixed 7.5-EC courses across disciplines. The comparison preserves Utrecht’s open profile space and does not pretend that UCR’s interdisciplinary breadth is the same curricular mechanism.
